comments.text: Two inverse screen-code digits copied into the status display; Mystery Maze file variants share number25.
Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 13. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 13 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 0; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 1500. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters '24'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn a life through $436A, poll status/input through $436D, and test bombs remaining at $3013. Zero bombs calls cleanup and jumps through completion vector $3030. Death mode 2 waits to become 0; reserves $40E4=$FF calls cleanup and jumps through exhaustion vector $3032, otherwise respawn. Cleanup vector $301D is invoked through a patched JSR.
IRQ collision callback: when player-active $402B and player collision mask $4088 are nonzero and player mode $4028 is 0, set mode 1 to begin death. Any colliding sprite is lethal here.

Drawing data $30A4-$3113 read by Initial scenery $30A4. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

13 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.

Drawing data $3170-$31A1 read by Post-bomb drawing $3170, Post-bomb drawing $317A, Post-bomb drawing $3184, Post-bomb drawing $318E, Post-bomb drawing $3198. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

Create at most seven followers. Select absolute read cursor200 if write cursor<8, else0; do not subtract a fixed common lag. Copy X-low/high,Y,frame from four history pages. CPU exhausts all256 creation cursors; early controlled cursor200 may read retained unfilled history, without proving a legal early pickup. Increment follower count$3241; enable the new sprite in colour1. Native joystick input reaches the first collection at X140/Y216, score100, one enabled follower at the historical X320/Y212 pose. A subsequent collection raises the count to two before ordinary death.

Replay runs before record: increment each follower cursor, then read its four history components. The modular cursor gap stays constant independently per follower. After replay/record, sample age is gap-1 once populated. CPU compares1100 ticks across wraps with seven followers.

During normal active play, write current player X-low/X-high/Y/frame into pages $3400/$3500/$3600/$3700 at cursor $324A, then increment the cursor modulo 256. Separate ordered callbacks record and replay the path.
Byte $3241 is follower count 0-7; the following seven bytes are read cursors for follower sprites 1-7. Creation initializes a cursor and replay advances it.
Unused eighth cursor-capacity byte between the seven follower cursors and the player recording cursor; no active index reaches it.
Modulo-256 history write index for player position/frame. Reset with all followers when death reaches mode 2.

At life2 disable active followers and reset count/write cursor. Preserve all1024 history bytes and individual read cursors. Life1 stops replay/record without this cleanup. CPU checked all states. A native two-follower death reaches this cleanup: both sprites are disabled, count and write cursor become zero, while read cursors remain33/6. The $3263 to $3269 counter-clear segment leaves all1,024 history bytes unchanged.
